summary.en: Maintain both directions when inserting, deleting and walking from either endpoint.
summary.bn: Insert, delete আর দুই দিক থেকে হাঁটার সময় next ও prev ঠিক রাখো।

notes: These implementations use C17. Compound literals and declarations in loop headers date from C99; C17 does not add automatic memory management.

examples.title: Insert after head, then remove that node
examples.explanationHtml: Insertion repairs the successor’s prev field as well as the predecessor’s next field. Removing the inserted node repairs both directions again.

examples.title: Walk from each endpoint
examples.explanationHtml: The forward walk follows next from head. The backward walk follows prev from tail, so a broken back link is easy to notice.

examples.title: Delete a singleton safely
examples.explanationHtml: Removing the only node changes both endpoints to NULL. The same unlink function also handles an already empty list.

examples.title: Insert after a known tail
examples.explanationHtml: At the tail there is no successor to repair. The new node becomes tail, while its prev field preserves backward traversal.

practice.title: Print both traversal directions
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16) and n values (-99..99). Print Forward: and Backward: lines.

practice.title: Delete the first node
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16) and n values (-99..99). Remove head if present, then print Forward: and Backward:.

practice.title: Delete the last node
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16) and n values (-99..99). Remove tail if present, then print Forward: and Backward:.
hints: Move tail to the predecessor before freeing.

practice.title: Insert after a chosen index
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16) and n values (-99..99). Read an index (0..n-1), then value (-99..99). For n=0 use index -1. Insert after that node, then print Forward: and Backward:.
hints: Repair next and prev at the insertion boundary.

quiz.prompt: For adjacent nodes A then B, which pair of links must agree?
options: A.prev == B and B.next == A always
quiz.explanation: Forward and backward relationships mirror each other. Values do not determine adjacency.

quiz.prompt: Given a valid node pointer, why is ordinary doubly linked deletion O(1)?
options: All lists have at most two nodes
Its prev and next identify both neighbors
quiz.explanation: Only a fixed number of fields change. Finding that node by value can still take O(n).

quiz.prompt: When deleting head, what must the new head’s prev become?
quiz.explanation: An ordinary non-circular list has no predecessor before head.

quiz.prompt: When inserting after tail, which endpoint changes?
quiz.explanation: The appended node becomes the final node. Head changes only for the empty-list convention.

quiz.prompt: Which extra cost distinguishes doubly from singly linked nodes?
quiz.explanation: prev makes backward traversal possible but adds storage and update obligations.

quiz.prompt: How do you remove a singleton with head and tail?
options: Leave head pointing to the old value
Set both endpoints to NULL, then free the node
Keep tail as a sentinel without allocating one
quiz.explanation: There are no neighbors to repair, and both endpoints refer to the victim.

quiz.prompt: Does having prev make search by value constant time?
options: Yes, every value is its address
Yes, prev is an index table
No, it can still inspect all n nodes
quiz.explanation: prev supplies local movement, not an index from values to nodes.

quiz.prompt: What value is reached by walking backward once from the second node?
quiz.explanation: b.prev identifies a, whose stored value is twelve. The backward link selects a different object from b.

quiz.prompt: After bypassing a middle node in both directions, which value is the tail predecessor?
quiz.explanation: Both bypass assignments connect a and c. Reading c.prev->value therefore reaches a’s twelve.

quiz.prompt: When both singleton endpoints clear, how many non-null endpoints remain?
quiz.explanation: Both endpoints are explicitly NULL, making both comparisons false. Their sum is zero.

quiz.prompt: Why can a correct forward print still hide a deletion bug?
options: next links are irrelevant to printing
A surviving prev may still refer to the removed node
quiz.explanation: Forward traversal reads next only. A stale backward link can remain invisible until a prev walk.

quiz.prompt: What extra work appears if a safe public deletion interface must find its node by value?
quiz.explanation: O(1) local unlinking assumes a valid node pointer is already available.

keyPoints.en: A doubly linked node stores both predecessor and successor links.
keyPoints.bn: ডাবলি লিংকড নোডে আগের আর পরের নোডের লিংক থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Neighbor links must agree after every completed doubly linked update.
keyPoints.bn: ডাবলি লিস্টে কাজ শেষে পাশের নোডগুলোর দুই দিকের লিংক মিলতে হবে।

keyPoints.en: Deleting a known node needs no search for its predecessor.
keyPoints.bn: নোড জানা থাকলে delete করতে তার আগের নোড খুঁজতে হয় না।

keyPoints.en: Endpoint deletion must update head or tail when the neighbor is absent.
keyPoints.bn: প্রান্তের নোড মুছলে পাশের নোড না থাকায় head বা tail বদলাতে হয়।

keyPoints.en: Backward traversal begins at tail and repeatedly follows prev.
keyPoints.bn: উল্টো দিকে হাঁটতে tail থেকে শুরু করে prev ধরে এগোও।

examQuestions.question: Insert X between A and B in a doubly linked list. State all four neighbor assignments.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Set X.prev=A and X.next=B. Set B.prev=X, then A.next=X. Before: A <-> B. After: A <-> X <-> B. At an endpoint, replace the absent-neighbor assignment with a head or tail update.

examQuestions.question: Give deletion steps for a known node cur with possible missing neighbors.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
if (cur->prev != NULL) {
    cur->prev->next = cur->next;
} else {
    *head = cur->next;
}
if (cur->next != NULL) {
    cur->next->prev = cur->prev;
} else {
    *tail = cur->prev;
}
free(cur);

examQuestions.question: Compare searching and deleting by value with deleting a known node.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Searching by value takes O(n) worst-case time in either list type. Once a doubly linked node is known, deletion uses its neighbors and takes O(1). Singly linked deletion generally also needs its predecessor or owning link. Doubly linked nodes pay for a prev field.
